I'm including some summer crops that are holding over reasonably well into cool fall weather here

Tomatoes - Seem to be doing a bit better (haven't really seen any blossom end rot) since I poured some water with crushed up tums (calcium carbonate) dissolved into it onto the plants, foliar and root feeding of calcium and raising the soil pH.

Zucchini - 3 zucchinis growing on it right now, and looks like possibly more to come soon, if all of these develop it'll be the best single round harvest from the plant so far

Romaine lettuce - Doing really well. All this shit needs is water and it's good to go. I mixed a healthy dose of all purpose organic fertilizer into the soil when I planted these.

Broccoli/cauliflower - Still not huge but they've only been going for just over a month, with barely acceptable part sun to boot. So they're doing fine.

Onions - These ailsa craig onions I planted a couple months ago to overwinter are doing very well. Nothing but consistent watering needed.

Beets - Still just sprouts, they'll take off more and more as weather cools and gets wetter though
